name: @openidentityplatform/ui-user
description: Open Identity Platform commons user UI — self-service and profile views, published as an ES module build and an AMD build from a single AMD source
//license: CDDL-1.1, matching @openidentityplatform/ui-commons and for the same reason: the repository's own LICENSE.md is authoritative over the per-file header boilerplate, which still names legal/CDDLv1.0.txt. build/npm-package.js copies ../../LICENSE.md into the payload and asserts that its heading names this version, so the declared identifier and the shipped text cannot drift apart. Reconciling the source headers is a repository-wide edit and stays out of scope for a build change.
//private: Kept deliberately per design decision D18. Phase 1 distributes this package as a Maven-attached tarball produced by `npm pack`, which honours "private"; only `npm publish` refuses. Task 3.11 removes this, after the phase-1 gate in 3.8.
//version: Must equal ${project.version} in commons/ui/user/pom.xml. Enforced by build/check-version.js, run by frontend-maven-plugin's `check-npm-version` execution at `initialize` (task 3.6): npm names the packed tarball from this field while build-helper-maven-plugin names the artifact it attaches from ${project.version}, so drift attaches a path that does not exist and fails at `install` with an unrelated message. The check is declared in the module pom, which merges after the parent's pluginManagement executions, so it runs just after `npm install` rather than before it - a drifted build therefore rewrites package-lock.json before failing. Accepted so that ui/mock, which has no such check to make, is not dragged in.
//exports: Emitted by build/npm-package.js, which omits the AMD build from the map on purpose — RequireJS and r.js never read package.json. Unlike ui-commons this package emits no "." entry: it has no aggregate module. ui-commons points "." at its main.js; there is no equivalent here, and inventing one would mean shipping an entry point no consumer of the AMD build has ever had.
//peerDependencies: Everything this package's modules import and does not itself contain. They are peers rather than dependencies because the consuming product composes commons by flat file overlay into one global namespace: a nested second copy means two module registries, not a subtle version skew. Versions are what the source is written against, from commons/ui/LIBS-INVENTORY.md (task 3.1).
//peerDependencies-ui-commons: DECIDED for task 3.3: this package DEPENDS ON @openidentityplatform/ui-commons rather than embedding it, and depends on it as a PEER. The Maven answer is the opposite — user/src/main/assembly/zip.xml copies target/dependency, the unpacked commons www, so commons.ui:user:zip:www is a superset and all five of its consumers (openam-ui-ria, openidm-ui-admin, openidm-ui-enduser, commons/selfservice/example-ui, commons/ui/mock) declare that one artifact and nothing else. Three things decided against carrying that shape into npm. (1) Sequencing: commons' ES module tree exists only in commons/target/npm and no Maven artifact carries it until task 3.6, so embedding the half that matters would mean reaching sideways into a sibling module's target/ directory or running a second copy of the emitter over commons' sources. (2) Single instance: 9 of these 14 modules import commons ids directly and all 12 under org/ reach them transitively (only the two config/ leaves have no dependencies at all), and commons is singleton-heavy — Configuration, EventManager, Router and the ESM LoaderRuntime seam all hold module-scoped state. Two copies means configure() lands on one seam while views resolve through the other, with no error anywhere. A peer forbids that by construction; a plain dependency permits npm to nest a second copy silently; embed cannot express it at all, because npm has no "conflicts with" and "install ui-user OR ui-commons, never both" would stay an unenforceable instruction. (3) The payload record: an embedded copy would put commons' 200 paths inside this module's build/expected-payload.txt, coupling it to every commons file change. The cost accepted in exchange: a consumer installs two packages, task 3.7 wires two tarballs and two copy steps, and the five zip consumers above each need a second declaration when they migrate. Ordering between the two copy steps is not a hazard — `LC_ALL=C comm -12` over the two payloads (128 commons paths against 45 here) returns zero collisions, so neither can overwrite the other, and the product's own sources still come last.
//peerDependencies-ui-commons-range: An exact version rather than a range. Both modules are built from one Maven reactor at one ${project.version} and are released together; there is no state in which a different commons version is the right one. Task 3.6's version-drift check keeps this honest on both sides, and task 3.12 is where a registry range replaces it.
//peerDependencies-lodash: `lodash` states TWO MAJORS rather than a single caret, for exactly the reason recorded in ui-commons' package.json — read that note first. Until task 8.3 this read `>=3.10.1`, because openam-ui-ria shipped lodash 3.10.1 at runtime while pinning 4.18.1 as a build-time devDependency, and lodash is the only one of these peers present in its npm tree at all; a bare `^3.10.1` would have made the packed tarball impossible to install into the sole phase-1 consumer — measured on ui-commons, ERESOLVE — which would have hard-failed task 3.7. TASKS 8.1, 8.2 AND 8.3 HAVE NOW RUN: this package's own call sites were rewritten, openam-ui-ria is on npm lodash 4.18.1 and the vendored 3.10.1 is deleted, so the range is now a real two-major compatibility claim rather than a placeholder. `>=3.10.1` is gone because it also admitted lodash 5, which nothing has tested. The lower bound stays at 3.10.1 because openidm-ui and openig-ui still consume commons through the commons.ui:*:zip:www Maven channel at that version. This package's Vitest suite passes against lodash 3.10.1 with 8.1/8.2's rewrites in place, which is evidence for the lodash 3 half of the range; see openam-ui-ria/NOTES-lodash-4.md. The two packages must state the same range or the conflict simply moves.
//peerDependencies-bootstrap: org/forgerock/commons/ui/user/profile/UserProfileView.js imports `bootstrap` for its tab behaviour. LIBS-INVENTORY.md row 12 records that the Maven artifact's `custom` classifier is a naming fiction: it is MD5-identical to bootstrap@3.3.5's own dist/js/bootstrap.js, so the npm package is an exact substitute with nothing to carry over.
//peerDependenciesMeta: OPTIONAL ONLY IN THE 'may be absent' SENSE, AND ONLY UNTIL TASK 3.11. This does NOT weaken the version guarantee, which is the reason it is acceptable here — measured against npm 10.9.7: with the peer absent, `npm install` succeeds instead of failing E404; with it present at 9.9.9 against this range, npm still refuses and goes looking for a matching version; with it present at 3.2.0-SNAPSHOT, it installs clean. So npm continues to forbid the second, mismatched copy that the peer declaration exists to prevent. What it gives up is the missing-peer warning. It is here because @openidentityplatform/ui-commons is on no registry until task 3.11, and without this flag npm cannot build a tree for this module at all: a plain `npm install` fails E404 on the unpublished peer, which would break the `npm install` execution frontend-maven-plugin binds at `initialize` and so the Maven build itself. `omit=peer` does not help — measured; npm resolves the peer edge even when omitting installation — and `--legacy-peer-deps` would suppress every peer check in the tree rather than this one, which is what ui-commons' package.json warns consumers not to do. Under D18 npm is not the channel commons arrives by during phase 1 anyway: task 3.7 installs both tarballs out of band. REMOVE THIS ENTRY in task 3.11, once ui-commons is published and a consumer's npm can actually resolve it.
//consumer-supplied-ids: Four identifiers these modules import that are NOT peers and cannot become peers. `underscore` is rebound by the product to lodash (openam-ui-ria's require.config.map), exactly as in ui-commons. `KBADelegate` is a logical name the product binds to its own implementation — openam-ui-ria points it at org/forgerock/openam/ui/user/services/KBADelegate, not at this package's own delegates/KBADelegate. And `form2js` and `js2form` have no npm package at all: LIBS-INVENTORY.md section 6 records both as maxatwork/form2js at a pinned git commit, never published — npm's `form2js` is a different fork's, and `js2form` is a sibling file in that same commit rather than a package. Declaring a peer range for any of the four would assert a resolution that does not exist. NPM-PACKAGE.md lists what a consumer binds each to, and `npm run verify:esm` fails if a fifth appears.
//devDependencies: The peer set repeated at the exact versions the source is written against, so this package can resolve its own specifiers without a consumer present — the ES module build cannot be imported to verify it otherwise. @openidentityplatform/ui-commons is absent on purpose: it is not on any registry yet (task 3.11), and build/verify-esm.mjs resolves it from the sibling module's emitted tree the way a consumer's alias will. Build-only entries: @buxlabs/amd-to-es6 generates the ES module tree from the AMD source, and @babel/* transpile the AMD tree — the same versions ui/commons pins, because ui/build/npm-package-lib.js runs both modules through one emitter and a version split there would mean two packages transpiled differently.
//devDependencies-esm-tests: vitest and jsdom are task 3.5's, and they close a gap build/verify-esm.mjs names in its own header: ten of this package's fourteen modules cannot be imported under bare Node, because commons' util/UIUtils assigns $.fn.emptySelect at module scope and jQuery 3 without a window carrying a document yields a factory with no .fn. That file says in as many words that the fix is jsdom and belongs to task 3.5, and declines to grow a stub until the import succeeds. src/test/vitest is that jsdom run: it imports all fourteen emitted ES modules, so the four verify-esm proves and the ten it cannot are both covered, and it does so against target/npm/esm rather than the sources. No `sinon` here, unlike ui/commons: this package has no behavioural suite to port — its one QUnit file is commented out of ui/mock's test list and runs on neither side — so nothing here stubs anything. Versions match ui/commons for the reasons recorded there: jsdom 30 needs Node >= 22.22.2 against frontend-maven-plugin's pinned 20.12.2, and vitest 4 would make `vite` a peer to declare and pin as well.
